cases.note: A company claim id is one token (shape 6)
A company versioned id is one token (shape 7); the query side adds no unversioned id
Company ids are one token each (shape 8), whatever the two-letter prefix
Six digits and ten digits are both the company id shape
Five digits are a near miss: no company shape applies, so it is the word cm and the number 12345
Eleven digits are a near miss: the longest match of shape 8 is followed by a digit, so the boundary fails and there is no backtracking; it is the word so and the number
On the index side a company versioned id is followed by its unversioned id
The Corpus claim shape fails the boundary on cl-xes-000012, so the company claim shape takes it; cl-cmp-0011 stays a Corpus claim id. Neither has extras
The conflict shape is tried first and takes xc-000042 whole, which is why no company family may use the prefix xc
ab-123456 has the company id shape whatever it means: the lexer carries no family list
Five digits: shapes 6 to 8 do not apply, so it is the word so and the number 00042
A trailing letter fails the boundary of shape 7, so shape 8 takes so-000042, which has no extras, and v2x is a word
